extracted.intended_audience: Applicants for T-1 nonimmigrant status, immigration practitioners (attorneys/representatives), and USCIS adjudicators
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative criteria for filing and adjudicating Applications for T Nonimmigrant Status (T-1) for victims of severe forms of trafficking in persons, including required evidence, bona fide review, physical presence, cooperation with law enforcement, hardship, numerical limits, and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS has sole jurisdiction over all applications for T nonimmigrant status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Applications for T Nonimmigrant Status must be filed with USCIS; USCIS adjudicates eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements (form and required evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant seeking T-1 nonimmigrant status must submit an Application for T Nonimmigrant Status on the form designated by USCIS in accordance with 8 CFR 103.2 and with the evidence described in paragraph (c) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must use the USCIS-designated form and include the initial evidence (detailed personal statement and supporting evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants in pending immigration proceedings must file directly with USCIS
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant in removal, exclusion, or deportation proceedings who wishes to apply for T-1 status must file an Application for T Nonimmigrant Status directly with USCIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICE may exercise prosecutorial discretion while USCIS adjudicates the application, including for derivatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants with final orders may file but filing does not preclude execution of order
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant subject to a final order of removal, deportation, or exclusion may file an Application for T Nonimmigrant Status directly with USCIS. Filing has no effect on DHS authority or discretion to execute a final order, though the applicant may request an administrative stay under 8 CFR 241.6(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If USCIS finds the application bona fide, the final order will be automatically stayed until final decision on the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS non-referral to removal proceedings absent serious aggravating circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS generally will not refer an applicant for T nonimmigrant status for removal proceedings while the application is pending or following denial, absent serious aggravating circumstances (e.g., egregious criminal history, national security threat, or complicity in trafficking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious aggravating circumstances may prompt referral despite a pending or denied application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor applicants — HHS notification
rubrics_metrics.description: When USCIS receives an application from a principal applicant under age 18, USCIS will notify the Department of Health and Human Services to facilitate provision of interim assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic referral to HHS to support minors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required detailed, signed personal statement
rubrics_metrics.description: An Application for T Nonimmigrant Status must include a detailed, signed personal statement from the applicant, in their own words, addressing specified topics about victimization and related matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal statement should address: nature of victimization; when it occurred; duration; how/when escaped or separated; events surrounding trafficking; who was responsible; circumstances of entry into U.S. if related to trafficking; how physical presence relates to trafficking; hardship and feared harm if removed; whether complied with reasonable law enforcement requests and existence of related records (or why age exemption/trauma exception applies). See § 214.204(c)(1)(i)-(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting evidence — any credible evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit any credible evidence that supports any of the eligibility requirements set out in §§ 214.206 through 214.209.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will consider all credible evidence; evidence types are listed throughout the regulations (e.g., affidavits, records, LEA declarations, medical records, news articles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadmissible applicants must request waiver of inadmissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is inadmissible to the United States, they must submit a request for a waiver of inadmissibility on the Application for Advance Permission to Enter as a Nonimmigrant (or successor form) in accordance with 8 CFR 212.16 and form instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow form instructions and regulatory waiver procedures; include supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEA declaration is optional and not conclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: An LEA declaration is optional evidence, is not given any special evidentiary weight, does not grant an immigration benefit, and does not lead to automatic approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEA declaration must be on the 'Declaration for Trafficking Victim,' signed by a supervising official responsible for detection, investigation, or prosecution of severe trafficking; completed at certifying official's discretion; does not require formal investigation or prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEA disavowal or withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: An LEA may disavow or withdraw a previously submitted declaration and should provide a detailed written explanation. After disavowal/withdrawal, the declaration generally will no longer be considered as evidence of compliance with law enforcement requests, but may be considered for other purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will treat disavowed LEA declarations accordingly when evaluating compliance or other aspects of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued Presence documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant granted Continued Presence under 28 CFR 1100.35 should submit documentation of the grant; if revoked it generally will no longer be considered as evidence of compliance with LEA requests but may be considered for other purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include documentation of grant or revocation when relevant to evidence of cooperation with law enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biometric services requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants for T-1 nonimmigrant status must submit biometrics in accordance with 8 CFR 103.16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide biometrics may affect adjudication or timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary standard and burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden is on the applicant to demonstrate eligibility for T-1 nonimmigrant status by a preponderance of the evidence. The applicant may submit any credible evidence relating to the application for consideration by USCIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will review all evidence, may investigate any aspect, may use evidence previously submitted for other benefits (but is not bound by prior factual determinations), and will determine evidentiary value in its sole discretion; USCIS considers the totality of the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona fide determination — initial review criteria (principal applicants)
rubrics_metrics.description: After initial review, USCIS will deem an Application for T Nonimmigrant Status bona fide if: (i) the applicant has submitted a properly filed and complete Application; (ii) the applicant has submitted a signed personal statement; and (iii) initial background checks are complete, have been reviewed, and do not present national security concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these three elements are present, USCIS may treat the application as bona fide and proceed accordingly (including stay of final orders and possible deferred action consideration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona fide determination — secondary/full review
rubrics_metrics.description: If initial review does not establish an application is bona fide, USCIS will conduct a full T nonimmigrant status eligibility review. An application that meets all eligibility requirements will be approved, or if the statutory cap has been reached, will receive a bona fide determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secondary review evaluates all eligibility requirements in depth and in order of receipt generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona fide determination for derivative family members
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a principal's application is deemed bona fide, USCIS will conduct an initial review for eligible family members in the United States; after initial review a derivative applicant is bona fide if: (i) the eligible family member is in the U.S. at time of determination; (ii) the principal or T-1 nonimmigrant has submitted a properly filed and complete Application for Derivative T Nonimmigrant Status; (iii) the application is supported by credible evidence that the derivative qualifies as eligible family member; and (iv) background checks are complete and not national security concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not established on initial review, derivatives proceed to full eligibility review; bona fide determination for derivatives may also be subject to the annual cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of bona fide determination and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: If USCIS determines an application is bona fide it will issue written notice informing the applicant they may be considered for deferred action and may file for employment authorization if not already filed; notice will inform that any final order is automatically stayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application is treated as bona fide as of the date of the notice; there are no motion or appeal rights for an initial bona fide determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not considered bona fide — incomplete or national security concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is incomplete or presents national security concerns, it will not be considered bona fide. There are no motion or appeal rights for a bona fide determination upon initial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications found not bona fide on initial review proceed to full eligibility review generally in order of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic stay of execution of final order when bona fide
rubrics_metrics.description: If USCIS determines an application is bona fide it automatically stays the execution of any final order of removal, deportation, or exclusion; the administrative stay remains in effect until any adverse decision becomes final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immigration judges and the Board lack jurisdiction to adjudicate a stay of removal on the basis of filing an Application for T Nonimmigrant Status or derivative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and evidence of being a victim of a severe form of trafficking
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must submit evidence demonstrating they are or have been a victim of a severe form of trafficking in persons (means and end for severe forms, except for sex trafficking of victims under 18), or if not performed labor/sex act must show they were recruited/transported/harbored/provided/obtained for purposes of subjection to trafficking or patronized/solicited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may satisfy this with personal statement (see § 214.204(c)) and other credible evidence (trial transcripts, court documents, police reports, news articles, reimbursement forms, affidavits, correspondence from trafficker, documents used in scheme, photographs, LEA declaration, Continued Presence documentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical presence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for T-1 status, an applicant must be physically present in the United States (including American Samoa, CNMI, or at a port-of-entry thereto) on account of such trafficking. USCIS considers presence at time of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant can demonstrate physical presence by showing they are currently being subjected to trafficking; were liberated by LEA; escaped before LEA; were trafficked in the past and current presence is directly related; or were allowed entry to participate in detection/investigation/prosecution. Presence is deemed regardless of where trafficking occurred; documentation required for participation entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence to establish physical presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must submit evidence demonstrating physical presence in the U.S. is on account of trafficking. USCIS will consider any credible evidence including: personal statement describing current presence and trauma; service provider records; documentation of stabilizing services; LEA declaration; Continued Presence documentation; documentation of entry or permission to remain; news reports, law enforcement records, court records; or any other credible evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal statement should address circumstances, health/psychological impacts, financial impact, access to services, cooperation with law enforcement, and relation of victimization to current presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to comply with any reasonable request for assistance from LEA
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible, an applicant must have complied with any reasonable request for assistance from an LEA in detection, investigation, or prosecution of trafficking acts, unless they meet an exception or exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At a minimum an applicant must contact an LEA with proper jurisdiction; credible evidence documenting a single contact may suffice; reporting may be telephonic, electronic, or other means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness of LEA requests — totality of circumstances factors
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant need only show compliance with reasonable requests; reasonableness depends on totality of the circumstances. Factors include but are not limited to: general law enforcement/prosecutorial practices; nature of victimization; specific victim circumstances; victim capacity/competency; trauma or risk of further trauma; access to support services; safety of victim/family; prior compliance; whether request would yield essential information; whether info could be obtained without victim; presence of interpreter/attorney; cultural/religious/moral objections; time to comply; age/health/maturity; any other relevant circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will weigh these factors when evaluating whether a request was reasonable and whether the applicant complied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence to show compliance with LEA requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must submit evidence demonstrating compliance with reasonable LEA requests, or evidence demonstrating an exception/exemption. Evidence can include: an LEA declaration, documentation of Continued Presence, affidavits of witnesses, or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Victim's statement should explain that an LEA with responsibility has information about trafficking, that the victim complied with reasonable requests, and, if not reported, why it was not previously reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception/exemption for inability to cooperate due to trauma
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant unable to cooperate with reasonable LEA requests due to physical or psychological trauma may be excepted or exempt; must submit credible evidence of trauma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence can include: personal statement describing trauma (age, background, maturity, health, disability, history), signed statement from qualified professional (medical/mental health/social worker/victim advocate), medical/psychological records, witness statements, photographs, police reports, court records/orders, disability determinations, government agency findings, or any other credible evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception/exemption for applicants under 18 at time of victimization
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who was under 18 at the time at least one trafficking act occurred is exempt from the requirement to comply with any reasonable request for assistance; must submit evidence of age at time of victimization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where available, include birth certificate, passport, or certified medical opinion; USCIS will consider any other credible evidence of age.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of established exception/exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant establishes that the exception or exemption applies, they are not required to have had contact with law enforcement or to comply with future requests, including reporting the trafficking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS retains authority and discretion to contact LEA when appropriate even if exception/exemption established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extreme hardship involving unusual and severe harm standard
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible, an applicant must demonstrate that removal would subject them to extreme hardship involving unusual and severe harm. A finding may be based on listed factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is encouraged to describe/document all relevant factors; no guarantee a particular reason will satisfy requirement; hardship to others considered only if it demonstrates applicant will suffer extreme hardship; evidence can include personal statements, country condition reports, and other credible sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for evaluating extreme hardship
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors include, but are not limited to: age/maturity/personal circumstances; physical or psychological issues needing care not reasonably available in foreign country; nature and extent of consequences of trafficking; impact of loss of access to U.S. courts/criminal justice for redress; reasonable expectation of severe penalization in foreign country for being a victim; likelihood of re-victimization and foreign authority protection; likelihood trafficker or associates would cause harm; threat from civil unrest/armed conflict; current or likely future economic harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit specific documentation to support each factor where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual numerical cap and waiting list
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS may not grant T-1 nonimmigrant status to more than 5,000 principal applicants per fiscal year. If the numerical limit prevents further grants, USCIS will place applicants who receive a bona fide determination on a waiting list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS assigns waiting list priority by date properly filed (oldest first); in the next fiscal year USCIS will issue a number to each waiting-list application in order; after issuing to waiting-list eligible applicants, remaining numbers issued to new eligible applicants by filing order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unlawful presence while on waiting list
rubrics_metrics.description: While an applicant for T nonimmigrant status in the U.S. is on the waiting list, the applicant will not accrue unlawful presence under section 212(a)(9)(B) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being on the waiting list preserves non-accrual of unlawful presence for that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal from the waiting list
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may be removed from the waiting list consistent with law and policy. Applicants must remain admissible and otherwise eligible for T nonimmigrant status; if USCIS receives information that an applicant is no longer eligible prior to final adjudication, the applicant may be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain admissibility and eligibility; update USCIS with material changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS decision, approval, and notification procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: After review USCIS will issue a decision approving or denying the application in accordance with 8 CFR 103.3. If approved, USCIS will grant T-1 status subject to annual limitation and provide evidence of status; may notify LEA and HHS/ORR as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with outstanding DHS removal orders have those orders deemed cancelled by operation of law as of USCIS approval date. Applicants with DOJ-issued orders may seek rescission via motion to reopen; ICE may exercise discretion to join motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment authorization incident to status
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual granted T-1 nonimmigrant status is authorized to work incident to status and does not need to file a separate Application for Employment Authorization to be granted employment authorization. USCIS will issue an initial EAD for the duration of T-1 status. Replacement EADs require filing an Application for Employment Authorization per form instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment authorization is ordinarily automatic upon grant of status; replacement procedures follow standard EAD rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance parole requirement for travel abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: To return to the United States after travel abroad and continue to hold T-1 nonimmigrant status, a T-1 nonimmigrant must be granted advance parole pursuant to section 212(d)(5) of the Act prior to departing the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain advance parole before departure to preserve ability to return in T-1 status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial effects and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon denial USCIS will notify the applicant per 8 CFR 103.3 and may notify LEA and HHS/ORR. If an applicant appeals a denial, the denial will not become final until the administrative appeal is decided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When denial becomes final, any benefits from a bona fide determination are revoked; prior termination of removal proceedings or stays may be reinstated; DHS may file Notice to Appear to place individual back into proceedings; stays on orders are lifted when denial is final.
